narrative.title: Doubling the Gear Ratio Instead of Cranking It
narrative.scenario: A press needs a mechanical ratio of x^n, and the operator only has a doubling jig: each crank squares the current ratio. Reading n in binary tells the operator exactly which squarings to bank — every 1 bit contributes the current squared value to the product, and negative exponents simply invert the finished ratio.
narrative.inputFormat: A double x and an integer n (possibly negative).
narrative.outputFormat: The value of x raised to the power n.
constraints: the result fits in a double

testCases.explanation: Ten is 1010 in binary: square-bank twice (4, then 256... ) — the product lands on 1024.
Three cranks of the base, no squaring shortcuts skipped: 2.1^3 = 9.261.

hintLevels: Level 1: n in binary is a recipe — every 1 bit means 'multiply the current squared base into the result'.
Level 2: Loop while n > 0: bank base when the low bit is 1, square base, shift n right.
Level 3: Negate-then-invert handles negative exponents, but watch INT_MIN: taking abs() of it overflows 32-bit ints, so widen first.
